newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy commission approves budget, moves to chamber.
newsitem.headline: Italy commission approves budget, moves to chamber.

text.p: The Chamber of Deputies (lower house) budget commission on Monday approved the centre-left government's 1997 budget, which now moves on to a debate in the full assembly.
The commission approved the draft budget by a vote of 25 for, 23 against, with one abstention.

The entire package, which aims to slash a massive 62.5 trillion lire ($42 billion) off next year's deficit, goes before the full chamber on Wednesday. It was drawn up in a hurried effort to win debt-burdened Italy membership of Europe's planned single currency from its launch in 1999.

Deputies will have until November 17 to vote on the budget after which it goes to the Senate (upper house) for ratification. The commission earlier on Monday approved a maxi-ammendment by Finance Minister Vincenzo Visco that grouped together a dozen articles concerning fiscal matters into a single clause.
The move could open the way for an eventual confidence motion in Visco's contested plans to reform Italy's creaking fiscal system.

Prime Minister Romano Prodi's government is facing stiff opposition to its budget plans and by fusing together various articles it would allow confidence motions to swiftly steam roller large chunks of the budget through parliament.
